The class has 200 students split into three groups.  
Let the size of each of the two equal larger groups be \(x\).  
The smallest group is 10 students fewer, so its size is \(x-10\).

The total number of students is therefore  

\[
x + x + (x-10) = 200 \;\Longrightarrow\; 3x - 10 = 200 \;\Longrightarrow\; 3x = 210 \;\Longrightarrow\; x = 70.
\]

Hence the smallest group contains  

\[
x-10 = 70 - 10 = 60 \text{ students}.
\]

All peer solutions reach the same conclusion, confirming the result.

**Final answer: 60**
